Eustyle: the space between 6 columns

Front held at 18 m. Metres are a modern scale choice, not a conversion from Roman feet.

Lower diameter: 1 m. Ordinary gap: 2.25 D. Central gap: 3 D. Column height: 9.5 m (9.5 D). Front between outer shaft faces: 18 m (18 D).

A clear gap excludes the shafts; an axis-to-axis bay includes one diameter as well. The drawing scale is shared by the five systems for these settings. Profiles are schematic. Bases, capitals, entasis, corner thickening and structural loads are not modeled.

Vitruvius III.3.6 · printed p. 65

namque facienda sunt in intervallis spatia duarum columnarum et quartae partis columnae crassitudinis, mediumque intercolumnium unum, quod erit in fronte, alterum, quod in postico, trium columnarum crassitudine

Make the ordinary spaces two column-thicknesses and a quarter; make the middle gap at the front, and the corresponding one at the rear, three column-thicknesses.

The central opening is an exception. Medium intercolumnium is the middle gap, not a middle column. This model follows the stated ordinary diameter before the later corner-thickening adjustment in III.3.11.

Vitruvius III.3.7 · printed p. 65

frons loci quae in aede constituta fuerit, si tetrastylos facienda fuerit, dividatur in partes XI S praeter crepidines et proiecturas spirarum; si sex erit columnarum, in partes XVIII; si octastylos constituetur, dividatur in XXIV et semissem

Divide the intended front into eleven and a half parts for four columns, excluding the steps and projecting bases; into eighteen for six columns; into twenty-four and a half for eight columns.

S abbreviates a half, semis. Each part becomes one lower column diameter. These totals include the columns themselves as well as the clear gaps. The numbers follow Krohn's printed text; his apparatus below records variant readings.

Vitruvius III.3.10 · printed p. 66

eustyli autem aedis columnae, uti systyli, in novem partes altitudo dividatur et dimidiam partem, et eius una pars constituatur in crassitudine imi scapi

For an eustyle temple, as for a systyle one, divide the column's height into nine and a half parts; make one part the thickness at the bottom of the shaft.

Altitudo is height; crassitudo is thickness or diameter here. Novem ... et dimidiam partem says nine and a half. The drawing uses this passage and the other four proportions in III.3.10, rather than silently substituting a different translation's number.

Greek word-parts

στῦλος (stylos): pillar, column. The recurring -style part belongs to the Greek word for a pillar. It is unrelated to a stylistic preference in the modern sense. Dictionary.

πυκνός (pyknos): close, compact. Pycno- describes close spacing. The same Greek word gives Pyknon, our separate experiment in close musical intervals. Dictionary.

σύν (syn): with, together. The first part of systyle is a form of this combining element. The architectural ratio comes from Vitruvius's definition, not from the word-part alone. Dictionary.

διά (dia): through; apart in compounds. Dia- can express separation in a compound. Here Vitruvius gives the numerical gap as three diameters. Dictionary.

ἀραιός (araios): sparse, not close-set. Araeo- describes wide separation. It does not itself specify four diameters or any other fixed number. Dictionary.

εὖ (eu): well. Eu- conveys a favorable judgment. Vitruvius prefers the eustyle arrangement; the name does not establish that every surviving temple followed it. Dictionary.

Vitruvius writes in Latin. These Greek headwords explain borrowed names; they are not a fabricated Greek version of his passage. English translations and teaching notes are new.
